subsystems.name: Pressurised rim habitat
subsystems.role: the living space at the outer edge, where centripetal acceleration stands in for gravity.
parts: floor and furniture rated for 1 g

subsystems.name: Rotating structure and spin joint
subsystems.role: holds the habitat at radius and lets it turn while the docking port stays still.
parts: low-leak rotary seal or non-contact bearing

subsystems.name: Attitude and spin control
subsystems.role: spins the structure up, holds it steady and stops it when needed.
parts: momentum wheels or control moment gyroscopes

subsystems.name: Radiation shielding
subsystems.role: protects the crew outside Earth's magnetic field, where there is no free shielding.
parts: regolith, if the habitat is built at a Moon or asteroid

subsystems.name: Closed-loop life support
subsystems.role: recycles air, water and eventually food for years without resupply.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal control
subsystems.role: runs the habitat and rejects the heat the crew and equipment make.
parts: solar arrays on the despun hub

buildSteps.title: Choose radius and spin rate together
buildSteps.detail: Comfort limits suggest staying below roughly 2 rotations per minute; producing 1 g at that rate needs a radius near 200 m, so large structures are unavoidable rather than a design choice.

buildSteps.title: Design for spin loads and pressure
buildSteps.detail: The structure must carry its own centripetal load and hold internal pressure; mass rises steeply with radius, so the mass budget drives every other decision.

buildSteps.title: Launch the pieces
buildSteps.detail: Ring segments, hub, truss and shielding are launched folded or in sections on heavy-lift rockets.

buildSteps.title: Assemble in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Robotic arms and spacewalking crews join modules and deploy the ring or tether, much as a space station is assembled today.

buildSteps.title: Fit the spin joint
buildSteps.detail: A rotating interface between the pressurised habitat and the stationary docking hub is installed — the hardest sealing and bearing problem in the machine.

buildSteps.title: Run uncrewed checkouts
buildSteps.detail: The structure is spun up slowly and its dynamics, balance and seal leakage measured before anyone lives aboard.

buildSteps.title: Commission with crew
buildSteps.detail: Crew move in at low gravity levels and the spin rate is raised over days while vestibular and cardiovascular responses are monitored.

buildSteps.title: Operate and escalate
buildSteps.detail: Resupply, maintenance and medical monitoring continue while gravity levels are tuned, and designers learn what fraction of Earth gravity is enough for health.

prerequisites.why: station modules have been joined in orbit, but nothing on the scale of a 100–200 m rotating ring.
existing rotary joints transmit power, not breathable air, and a pressurised seal must turn for years without leaking.
ground centrifuges and the Gemini 11 tethered-spin experiment (1966) showed the effect works, but no crew has lived at continuous artificial gravity for months.
water and air are recycled on orbit today, but food production and multi-year reliability are unproven.
shielding mass competes directly with the structural mass a spinning habitat already demands.
large mass must be lifted cheaply and manoeuvred into the assembly orbit.

pathway.milestone: ground-based short-radius centrifuge and bed-rest studies pin down the rotation rates people can tolerate
pathway.unlocks: numbers that fix the minimum radius of any future habitat.

pathway.milestone: an uncrewed spinning tether or ring segment demonstrated in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the structure can be deployed, stabilised and controlled.

pathway.milestone: a small human-tended spinning module attached to a station, occupied for weeks
pathway.unlocks: the first medical data on partial gravity sustained over time.

pathway.milestone: a free-flying artificial-gravity station with closed-loop life support
pathway.unlocks: a testbed for long-duration habitation without resupply.

pathway.milestone: a rotating transit vehicle for a Mars mission, either a full ring or a tether between crew module and counterweight
pathway.unlocks: removes the largest medical unknown from multi-year voyages.
